taken.mechanism: A plan is a living document that a reader with only the plan and the working tree can resume from; it is revised as work moves rather than written once.
Required living sections: progress split into done and remaining at every stop, surprises and discoveries backed by a short piece of evidence, and a decision log that says why the plan changed.
Acceptance phrased as behaviour someone can observe, for an internal change a test that fails before and passes after.
Idempotent steps with a retry or rollback path for anything risky, backups before destructive steps, and additive changes with a parallel old path during a migration.
Prototype milestones that de-risk an unknown, with explicit criteria for promoting or discarding the prototype.

rejected: 'Resolve ambiguities autonomously' and 'do not prompt the user for next steps': product choices belong to the user, and westack's authority rules govern; open questions are asked with a recommended answer.
Prose-only plans with checklists only in Progress: the plangraph format needs per-slice fields, so slices are structured and the narrative sits in Context.
Progress checkboxes as the record of done: done comes from receipts, never a ticked box.

donors.licence: Apache-2.0

taken.mechanism: Research the codebase before asking the user anything, and ask only what investigation cannot answer; check a user's correction against the code before accepting it.
Each phase's success criteria split into automated checks an agent can run and manual checks only a person can confirm; manual ones stay open until the person confirms.
An explicit list of what the plan will not do, against scope creep.
Deviations from the plan reported separately from defects.
Research that describes the system as it is, with file:line references, before judging it.
When reality differs from the plan, stop and state expected, found and why it matters, rather than pressing on.

rejected: On resume, trust checked-off work and verify only if something seems off (r2:N20): done comes from current receipts; the last done slice's check is re-run on resume.
No open questions at all in the final plan: a plan may carry an assumption the user explicitly accepted, labelled; an approved plan carries no open decision (plangraph enforces it).
Tool-specific steps (thoughts sync, named research agents, make targets).

donors.licence: MIT

taken.mechanism: Tracer-bullet tickets: each a narrow slice across the layers it touches that can be demonstrated alone; prefactoring in its own first ticket; sized for one fresh session.
Requirement coverage: a breakdown counts as complete only once each requirement still in force has a ticket delivering it, and each constraint is carried or explicitly deferred.
Milestones as ordered phases with a goal, each leaving the product working; a blocker may not sit in a later phase than the work it blocks.

Stable identities across re-runs: existing tickets and milestone names are kept, changed requirements are pointed out, native tracker ids are recorded separately from phase numbers and never assumed from a name match.

Nothing is created in the tracker until the user approves the breakdown; creation in dependency order so blockers carry real ids; read back to verify; on an uncertain call stop, report and reconcile before retrying.

Local markdown tickets as the fallback (one file per ticket, numbered in dependency order, Status and Blocked-by lines), with per-tracker mappings for dependencies and phases on GitHub, Jira and Linear.

rejected: Setting created tickets to a 'ready' status and treating tracker status as progress: status is a marker; done comes from receipts.
Requirements and tickets kept in a feature requirements.md registry: the plan file is the one record; westack adds no second store.

donors.licence: MIT

taken.mechanism: A plan records the decisions the implementer cannot make alone (files, names, signatures, pinned values, the tests that prove each task) and leaves out what the signature and test already fix; a plan longer than its code has written the code, and lines that decide nothing are gaps.
Per-task interfaces: what a task consumes from earlier tasks and produces for later ones, with exact names, checked for consistency across the plan.
A self-review pass before handing over: requirement coverage, name consistency and proportion.

rejected: Two-to-five-minute steps with full code bodies for every task: granularity follows size here (tiny none, bounded a slice list, cross-cutting a living plan).
A commit at every step: commits are the user's grant, not a planning default.

donors.licence: MIT

taken.mechanism: A computed ready set: the work whose blockers are all finished, derived from the dependency graph rather than kept by hand.
Work discovered mid-task is filed as a new item linked to where it was found, instead of silently widening the current item.

rejected: Closing an item with a free-text reason as the record of done: in westack-plan a slice is done only with a receipt per criterion; the ready set counts only those.
A separate issue database: when a repository already uses Beads, the core defer map's convention entry applies; otherwise the plan file is the record.

taken.mechanism: Planning is non-mutating: reading, searching and checks that write only caches are allowed; edits to tracked files are not, and a request to execute while planning is handed on rather than done.
Two kinds of unknown: discoverable facts are explored before asking; preferences and trade-offs are asked early with a few options and a recommended default, which may stand as a recorded assumption.

rejected: Plan mode that persists until the host ends it and a special proposed-plan block: host-specific; the report's first line carries the plan state instead.
Discouraging file paths in the plan: slices name their paths so scope and diff audits can be checked.

own_additions: Done never comes from ticket text, enforced in the checker: a done slice needs a receipt reference for every criterion, and a human-only criterion a person's confirmation; anything else is reported as claimed_done and its dependants stay waiting.
Consumers as a first-class slice field, found by searching the whole repository for the changed contract, each with its own acceptance criterion.
A rollback table in proportion to the kind of change, with 'none' refused and 'irreversible' needing approval at build time.
An approved plan may carry no open decision (checked).
One vocabulary with the task record: slice statuses are the contract's work_unit statuses, read from the core contract when present, so a markdown plan maps onto work_units, acceptance and decisions.
A one-slice hand-off note to westack-build or westack-tdd, so a chain does not carry the whole planning conversation.

helper_decision.reason: Three of this skill's rules are claims about a plan's structure that drift as a plan is edited and re-planned: the dependency graph (cycles, missing or out-of-phase blockers), completeness (every slice has acceptance and rollback, every requirement a slice) and done-from-receipts (the ready set may count only slices with a receipt per criterion). A standard-library reader checks them deterministically, runs nothing and writes nothing, and computes the ready set the map-review asked to derive from evidence rather than status text.
helper_decision.reuse: A task record (.json) is read through the core's record.py: record.shape checks it against contract.json, and slice statuses come from the contract's work_unit enum. The cycle check is not reused because record.py keeps it inside check_task, which needs a complete record and an evidence root; markdown plans have no record, so the checker carries a small graph routine of its own and leaves the record's full consistency to validate.py task.
helper_decision.tests: tests/test_plangraph.py, 40 tests: red against a signature-only stub (34 failed, 1 error, 5 absence checks passed), then green; five broken copies (cycle check off, done from status text, human-only rule off, coverage off, ready set ignoring dependencies) each killed on assertions, judged by westack-tdd controls.py (verdict supported).

overlap_check.method: lower-cased word 12-grams of every text file in this package (SKILL.md, references, scripts, tests, provenance, evals) against all 22 fetched donor files, licences included; any shared 12-gram is a flag, extended to its full run
